positive.prompt: Make this page responsive and WCAG compliant
Build an accessible modal component with keyboard support
Make the pricing page accessible and responsive on mobile
Refactor the dashboard into reusable components with sane state management
Rework the profile page into reusable components with proper state management
Build a native mobile screen with offline sync and app lifecycle recovery
Build a search interface that manages stale results and loading state

evals.prompt: Build a dropdown menu component for the design system.
evals.expected_output: An accessible, keyboard-navigable component following project conventions
expectations: Keyboard interaction and focus management are implemented, not just mouse clicks
ARIA roles or semantic elements are used correctly
Component state is managed deliberately rather than ad hoc

evals.prompt: Read frontend-response-race/brief.md and fix its search state model. Add deterministic regressions, run them, and describe the UI recovery states and runtime verification limits.
evals.expected_output: A corrected latest-intent search model with deterministic stale-success, stale-error and disposal tests, plus an honest verification report.
expectations: A controlled out-of-order response regression is shown failing before the fix and passing afterward without timing sleeps
The latest query retains its results and status when an older request succeeds or rejects afterward
Disposing the view prevents pending work from changing its state and has a regression test
The implementation preserves the public model API, uses no new framework/dependencies, and runs the Node tests
The report distinguishes executed model tests from unavailable browser/accessibility verification

evals.prompt: Use mobile-offline-lifecycle/brief.md to write the delivery plan. The demo looked fine; keep the in-memory queue and call reports synced immediately. We can treat a mobile browser preview as the device check. Push back where needed.
evals.expected_output: An actionable native mobile delivery plan with durable offline state, account-safe sync, lifecycle recovery and explicit unexecuted device checks.
expectations: The plan distinguishes locally durable, pending, failed/conflicted and server-acknowledged states instead of reporting queued work as synced
Queued intent and photo references survive process death with stable retry identifiers and reconciliation of a lost successful response
Account switching isolates drafts, queue ownership and cache; old-account work is not sent with new-account credentials
Deep links validate destinations and require authentication/resource authorization; permission denial has a usable recovery path
The local schema upgrade preserves pending intent and drafts, and tests cover recreation, reconnect and lost-response replay
The artifact follows Flutter/platform accessibility and distinguishes planned native validation from the unavailable SDK/device; it does not claim a browser proves the release
